newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Feb 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The first head-on challenge to the Australian Stock exchange's monopoly is on the way with The Sydney Futures Exchange planning to launch a share trading system. Over the last 18 months the SFE has been developing an electronic shares system called LOCAM, an acronym for Large Order Call Market, aimed at institutional investors. Page 1.

Qantas Airways revealed yesterday it had held its own in a turbulent December half, stamping its dominance over rival Air New Zealand-Ansett in the regional market by maintaining its profit base in the face of a collapse in earnings from Japan. The group drew on A$237 million in internal savings to eke out a 2.4 per cent higher net profit of A$151.6 million. Page 33.

The British Government yesterday released Foster's Brewing Group's UK pub chains from an obligation to free its 2,900 pubs from tied beer supply arrangement with Scottish and Newcastle from March 1998, finalising the restructuring of Foster's. Analysts suggested the decision would see Foster's seel its 50 per cent interest or float the company. The removal of the constraints on beer supply from S&N, which acquired Foster's UK brewing operations in 1995, has removed a potential hurdle to any brewer interested in cquiring BHP's 37 per cent shareholding in the company. Page 33.

As Air New Zealand scours Europe and Asia for additional airline partners to bolster its potentially powerful alliance with Ansett and United Airlines, the future of Qantas' 19.4 per cent stake in Air New Zealand continued to be questioned yesterday. Charman Gary Pemberton again denied the shareholding was on the market and insisted that Qantas' eight-year-old investment had not changed at all and no attempts were being made to offload the valuable tranche of "B" shares. Page 33.

As evidence of a split emerged yesterday among institutions over BIL's acquisition plan Brierley Investments Limited's chance of moving to 25 per cent of John Fairfax Holdings Limited improved. Fairfax shareholders will be asked to vote at a meeting in Sdney today whether BIL, which owns 20 per cent of the company, should be allowed to acquire another 5 per cent without making a takeover bid. Page 35.

The MasterIndex of Consumer Confidence released by Mastercard International yesterday, surveyed 13 countries in the Asia-Pacific region and ranks Australia behind China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore and Thailand regarding consumrs optimism about their future. Australia rated a score of 57.2 with good expectations of regular incomes 75.6 and the economy 60.7. Confidence in the sharemarket has slipped but remained hight at 60 points, employment 45.3 and peoples quality of life oer the next six months 44.3. Page 2.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Expectations of an acceleration in economic activity this year and a flow-on improvement in business earnings and investment were sparked yesterday by record levels in corporate profits in the December quarter. Australian Bureau of Statistics figures relased yesterday showed company reports of seasonally adjusted profits before interest, tax and depreciation of A$12.02 billion. The result represented a solid 9.9 per cent gain on the corresponding quarter of 1995 and was the highest score reported since th ABS began publishing corporate earnings in September 1985. Page 21.

RTZ-CRA's partner in the Diavik diamond project, just south of BHP's A$1.1 billion Diamet diamond mine at Lac de Gras, Canada, has upgraded the value of the discovery. Independent valuation in Antwerp of diamonds by Canadian mining house Aber Resources Ltd and RTZ-CRA has resulted in an 11 per cent increase in the average value of gems produced from the test drilling. Page 23.

Qantas announced yesterday an unexpected 2.1 per cent increase in the interim profit, despite bottom-line losses of more than A$50 million caused by higher fuel costs and a collapse in earnings from the market of Japan. Calling in a A$151.4 million net pofit for the last half of the year, chairman Gar Pemberton remained cautious on the full-year outlook and set much of the interim profit was due to an aggressive cost-cutting program which delivered A$237 million in savings. Page 21.

Fledgling Sausage Software Ltd's A$1.9 million net loss has been attributed to the expense involved in establishing its software business. Managing director Steve Outrim said the half-year result was within A$150,000 of its budget, the board would scale own and sack staff associated with its simple applications product and pursue opportunities in electronic commerce. Page 22.

Upmarket department store David Jones Ltd's decision to exit its John Martin's stores was applauded by the stock market yesterday, but DJs warned warned that the company was not in the clear just yet. DJ's shares moved up 8 cents to A$1.64 with analysts saying DJs management could now focus solely on problems in the stores - to regain sales. Page 22.

The outcome of Optus Vision shareholders' offer to the Seven Network to buy them out of Optus for as little as A$534 million , is expected to be announced today. It is believed Seven will formally accept the offer, lifting the stakes in its

legal battle wth Optus Vision. The move, however, would only be valid if Seven wins its claim against Optus shareholders for breaching its shareholding agreement by allowing the Packer family's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd to lift its options in Optus Vision. Page23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Qantas Airways shares flew to a record high of A$2.48 yesterday as the air carrier overcame a highly competitive market to post a 2.1 per cent rise in net profits to A$151.4 million for the half year to December. Total revenue for the
group was up 2.5 percent to A$3.97 billion. Page 27.

According to analysts the death of China's paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping, is unlikely to cause any major hiccups for Australian companies doing business there. Director of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council in Sydney, Ralph Chow, said people were pepared for his death. Meanwhile directors of Australian companies do not predict any change to operations in China. Page 27.

Insurance group MMI is looking to expand in Asia following a 20 per cent increase in net profit to A$18.1 million in the December half. MMI is looking for help for the move from its major shareholder, Allianz, as it aims to set a joint-venture general insrance business. Page 29.

Construction and engineering group, Leighton Holdings revealed an 18 per cent increase in interim profit yesterday citing increasing activity in Australia's non residential building sector. For the December half-year, Leighton delivered A$32 million afterabnormals up from A$27
million in the previous corresponding period. Page 29.

Colonial State Bank has signed a half-billion dollar deal to outsource all the banks information technology, communications, development and operations. The A$532 million seven-year contract is with a small US group, Alltel Information Services. Page 28.

Diversified food ingredients group Burns, Philp and Co has again dipped into its superannuation fund to achieve an 18 per cent rise in net profit to A$48.2 million in the December half. However the profit result failed to inspire stockbroking analysts who claimed the result was poor quality and there was an ambiguity as to where sustainable earning would come from. Page 27.
THE AGE

Australian international air-carrier, Qantas, is urgently trying to resurrect profits from its once-lucrative Japanese routes after a A$150 million drop in their profit contributions in recent years. Meanwhile the Japanese problems, added with a A$50 millon rise in fuel costs held Qantas to a 2.1 per cent increase in December half-year profits to A$151.4 million. Page C1
Shares in Melbourne's Crown Casino fell yesterday as brokers began to downgrade the profit forecast for Crown. Crown shares closed eight cents lower at A$2.40. Page C1.

Asia's export slump and the rising Australian dollar added to slow growth in Australia's exports to East Asia during 1996. The Australian Bureau of Statistics revealed a 3 per cent growth rate for the region during the period, a rate which is one-third ofits average in recent years. Page C1.

Following a stunning listing on the Australian Stock Exchange in October last year, Sausage Software yesterday sacked almost a third of its work force and dramatically downgraded its full year forecasts after reporting a A$1.9 million
December-half loss. After a period of soul searching, Sausage will now focus its energies on its electronic commerce division and Internet commerce. Page C1.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia has moved to show its dominance on the small business market with the launch of a lending facility that undercuts leading rivals. The CBA launched credit facility, Capital Equity, includes an interest rate on debit balancesof 7.55 per cent and comes just a day after the ANZ Banking Group committed A$1 billion to similar product with an interest rate fixed at 7.9 per cent. Page C3.

Investment markets dropped yesterday with bonds and futures weakened by offshore selling. Benchmark November 2006 Commonwealth bonds rose 13 points to 7.42 per cent while April 2000s gained 10 points to 6.73. Dealers said the release of data showing a 86 per cent rise in net corporate profits to A$12 billion in the last quarter also weakened the market. Page C2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
